title: Grateful Dead Live at Danish Center on 1966-03-12
taper: Source disc provided by Terry Doherty

ai_review.summary: Fair‑quality audience tape of the 3/12/66 Acid Test era show, highlighted by a stellar One Kind Favor and early‑era Viola Lee Blues despite mix imbalances.
ai_review.review: The recording captures a rare 1966 performance that many reviewers find musically exciting – Jerry’s surfy guitar runs, Bob’s embryonic lead style on One Kind Favor, and a solid rhythm section. The tape suffers from balance problems (Jerry too forward, Phil, Bob and Bill often buried) and occasional cuts, giving it an overall fair sound quality but still worth listening to for its historic value.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical performance (average show rating ~4) while noting notable recording flaws (average recording rating ~3). The mix of positive and critical comments yields a mid‑range overall score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Imbalance in the mix – Jerry’s guitar overly loud, Phil, Bob and Bill often muffled; low volume overall with occasional cuts typical of mid‑60s audience tapes.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early Acid Test set with solid playing throughout; a few moments feel slightly disjointed but the energy stays high, especially in the blues numbers.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Guitar is very loud and surf‑y; runs are impressive but dominate the mix.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is often muffled and disappears when volume is lowered due to poor balance.
band_member_comments.Bob: Shows his nascent lead‑guitar style on One Kind Favor; generally buried in the mix.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith (Pig) delivers strong organ, vocals, and harmonica work, though at times masked by the imbalance.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s drumming is present but can disappear when the overall volume is reduced because of mixing issues.
